newsitem.title: UK: UK corporate liquidations edge up in Q3 - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK corporate liquidations edge up in Q3 - survey.

text.p: The number of British companies going into liquidation edged up in the three months to September, while personal bankruptcies were little changed, accountancy firm KPMG said on Monday.
The number of corporate liquidations rose to 3,380 in the third quarter, from 3,299 in the second quarter.
Within that figure, 1,246 were compulsory liquidations and 2,134 were creditors voluntary liquidations.
Personal bankruptcies totalled 5,446 in the third quarter, an increase of only three from the previous three months.
"We have entered a period of stability, where the rate of failure will stay relatively level," said Mike Wheeler, head of corporate recovery at KPMG.
"I do not believe that the small increase in interest rates will have an effect on levels of insolvency, and I, like many others, will be looking to the Chancellor's budget to maintain the recovery."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will present his budget on November 26.
